A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same zero/one-layer progressive-training work despite the changed title. All 20 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A-C, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT2 and nanoMoE training experiments on OpenWebText, ResNet experiments on ImageNet, and initialization, scheduling, and optimizer ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for LLAMA3, Qwen3, Mixtral, and DeepSeekV3, scaling-law fits, and optimizer-switching experiments.

M1.justification: The expansion rules, Muon-NSGD updates, and Section 7 training recipe remain intact. Appendix C.3 adds an optional training variant that switches from NSGD or AdamW to Muon-NSGD at depth expansion; v1's optimizer comparisons kept the optimizer fixed.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate language models on OpenWebText and image classifiers on ImageNet. The additional model architectures and scaling sweeps retain these data and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 19 introduces standalone NSGD source-model comparisons and NSGD/AdamW-to-Muon-NSGD transitions against Muon-NSGD controls. v1 Appendix C.5 compared AdamW and Muon-NSGD across schedules. The shorter fixed-size baseline in v2 Section 3.4 already appeared in v1 Appendix C.1.

E3.justification: v2 adds four LLM architecture configurations, 16-layer expansion tests, and scaling experiments with specified model-size ranges and token-to-parameter ratios of 50 and 100. Figure 19 adds optimizer-switching protocols at different expansion times. Section 2 also revises the stated weight decay from 0.1 to 0.01, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds scaling-law analyses and optimizer-switching ablations and extends initialization comparisons across additional architectures. It removes the ResNet initialization and ordering plots from v1 Figures 2 and 4. The shorter-training and single-stage-versus-multistage analyses are retained and moved into the main text.

E5.justification: New Figure 2 reports fitted power-law parameters and R-squared goodness-of-fit statistics, ranging from 0.991 to 0.999. Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds scaling-law results, including LLAMA3 zero-layer and fixed-size exponents of -0.241 and -0.218, additional architecture convergence results, and optimizer-switching outcomes. It replaces nanoMoE results with DeepSeekV3 results and removes ResNet initialization/ordering results. The headline GPT2 curves and reported savings in Figure 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 changes from bounding averaged-iterate loss using Jensen's inequality to bounding last-iterate loss with an additional schedule-dependent term attributed to Defazio et al. (2023). v1 Equation 4.5's explicit loss-gap inequality is replaced by an empirically motivated comparison of upper bounds in v2 Section 4.2. These substantially revise the central mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add a scaling-law claim of approximately 3-5 times greater compute efficiency on LLAMA3 and DeepSeekV3, with advantages increasing at larger scales. This extends the central contribution beyond v1's GPT2 acceleration and zero/one-layer tradeoff claims, which remain.

C2.justification: Takeaway 2 replaces the categorical function-preservation-to-non-muP implication with a qualified warning that zero initialization can block feature learning. Section 4.2 newly motivates interpreting upper-bound differences as actual-loss differences, while Appendix C.3 discusses cheaper first-stage optimizers and possible further convergence with longer training.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds hidden/intermediate dimensions, attention-head counts, weight tying, and other architecture details for the new LLM experiments. However, v2 omits v1's explicit 120k-step control schedule details and the former nanoMoE expert-count and auxiliary-loss specification. The existing GPT2 and optimizer implementation descriptions largely remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the new architectures and their components, SOLAR depth upscaling, and the revised theoretical argument, including Defazio et al. (2023) and Bu et al. (2026). References to STEP, nanoMoE, OpenMoE, and ST-MoE are removed. The overall positioning against earlier progressive-training approaches remains similar.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, edits the abstract and contributions, divides Section 4 into two subsections, and moves v1 Appendices C.1 and C.3 into Sections 3.4 and 6. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds scaling-law and optimizer-switching figures, expands the initialization display to five architecture panels, and removes ResNet panels. Several retained plots are substantially enlarged and rearranged, notably the schedule and loss-compute figures, while appendix controls move into the main text. Both tables retain their contents.

improvement.justification: Figures 2-3 substantially strengthen evidence that the approach transfers beyond GPT2/nanoMoE to newer dense and MoE architectures and clarify how compute efficiency varies with scale. The optimizer-switching study and more readable figures add practical value. The largest-scale savings rely on extrapolated fits, and some ResNet analyses and reproducibility details are lost, but the broader direct experimental support provides a substantial net improvement.
